about: Machine-readable changelog of @origingame/engine (docs/release.md §3). kind: patch (0.x.y, compatible) or minor (0.x.0, has breaks). simulation: changed when a game's world can step differently (the golden replays' hashes moved, scripts/replay-gate.ts), else unchanged; versions before 0.6.1 were not measured and say changed. breaking: what a game may have to edit, each with the fix; find lists the identifiers og upgrade searches the game's sources for, codemod a mechanical rewrite it applies. CHANGELOG.md has the prose.

added.summary: The IDL takes an `aliases "..."` line on functions, records, structs, enums, unions and interfaces: synonyms and other engines' names (Unity, Godot, Unreal, three.js). The wiki prints it as `Also known as:` and `og api find` scores it as a fifth BM25F field; field lengths now average over the entries that have the field. 94 entries carry aliases, and a few one-line docs gained their purpose (defineSystem, og.SensorEntered). On the 160-query evaluation set recall@1 goes from 53 to 62 and recall@5 from 100 to 132; on a 40-query held-out set written before any alias and never tuned against (crates/og-cli/tests/fixtures/api-find-heldout.tsv) recall stays at 9 to 10 @1 and 21 @5: aliases fix the entries they name, not others.

`og api find` fuses BM25F with static word embeddings by reciprocal rank (k 20, embedding weight 0.7), so a query worded by purpose finds entries none of its words names. The model is minishlab/potion-base-8M (model2vec, MIT, third_party/potion-base-8M) cut to 128 dimensions and int8 (crates/og-api/search/words.bin, 4.1 MB, compiled into og); each entry's vector is built at `og api gen` and shipped in wiki/search.tsv. CPU only, no service. On the evaluation set, grown to 160 queries (crates/og-cli/tests/fixtures/api-find-queries.tsv), recall@1 rises from 46 to 53 and recall@5 from 90 to 100 over BM25F alone. The line output is unchanged; `--json` adds each entry's `bm25` and `cosine` beside the fused `score`.

Identical cooked outputs share the filename of the lexicographically smallest asset id. Bundle source lookup uses a map, and web preloading fetches shared files once. Cook stamps changed: the first cook after upgrading rebuilds everything. Content hashes no longer include the source pathname; actions that resolve relative references or embed asset names retain their path dependency. The same inputs and cooker still produce byte-identical cooked files. The blob format and FNV stamp algorithm are unchanged.

added.member: probe pickUi (wire pick_ui), PickResult.source and PickResult.ui
added.summary: pickUi(x, y) answers the UI element under a point: the topmost that shows something or takes input (a layout container that draws nothing lets the point through), with its id, path, kind, text, rect, layer, the document line that built it (source), the style part it is drawn as and the style rules that dress it, each with its file and line in the order they apply (rules; rule the most specific). pick keeps its scene answer; its source now names the scene line that declares the entity (scenes/main.ogt:12), and outside a publish build it carries the UI element over the point as ui. dump_ui's elements carry part and rules too.

`og assets` queries the unshipped cooked/.assets.ogt metadata and reference graph by text, --kind, --group and --unused. --refs lists dependencies, --by lists referrers, --dupes finds identical outputs and --dupes --near N compares texture dHashes and sound loudness-envelope hashes at the caller's Hamming threshold. --json returns structured results. Game TypeScript is parsed with OXC; computed og.load paths retain their static prefix, or everything without a prefix, and are reported. `og api find` discovers the assets guide.

og assets mv <from> <to> moves a source and its import settings, rewriting matching static asset-id literals in OGT documents and game TypeScript. Computed loads are reported, not rewritten. Destinations must be absent; parsing and path checks precede staged writes with rollback backups. Source-relative dependencies inside models and maps still need review when moving across directories. Run og cook afterward to refresh outputs.

Native cooks share BLAKE3 action keys and authenticated contents under ~/.cache/origingame/cook-v1/{ac,cas}, including texture and content-keyed prefracture results. A per-project .og/cook-index records file stats and content hashes and skips source reads on unchanged cooks. The store defaults to a 10 GiB cap, configurable with OG_COOK_CACHE_MAX_BYTES; og cache gc [--max-bytes N] [--json] trims it on demand. Cache eviction never deletes source assets or cooked outputs. FNV world/schema hashes and in-blob stamps, streaming packs and service-worker SHA256 remain unchanged.

Publish exports omit unreachable cooked outputs and list omitted ids, removed files and computed-load retention in og-build.json's pruning field. Project asset references, placed scenes, TS literals and publish { keep "path/**" } patterns are roots. Computed loads retain their static prefix or all assets; escaped loaders and runtime-keyed baked probes are kept conservatively. Needed streaming packs keep every member without changing pack bytes. Shared files survive while any retained id names them. Source assets and development cooked files are never deleted by export pruning.

`og api find` ranks with BM25F over each entry's name, summary, member names and body (camelCase, snake_case and dotted names split, plurals and -ing/-ed stemmed, a word one or two edits off still matching), from an index `og api gen` ships beside the wiki (wiki/search.tsv); a query takes milliseconds with no service. On the 96-query evaluation set (crates/og-cli/tests/fixtures/api-find-queries.tsv: queries by purpose, partial name and typo) recall@1 rises from 18 to 30 and recall@5 from 38 to 56. `--json` prints the entries with their scores; the line output and `og api show` are unchanged, and `og api show <module>` lists the module's members after its overview. The wiki is split: a module page keeps its overview, values, constants and a contents table (signature and one sentence per item), and every function, record, interface and type has its own page under wiki/<module>/ (ui.md 1.1 MB to 116 KB, render.md 0.6 MB to 54 KB).

Guides beside the IDL (crates/og-api/guides: start, testing, determinism, looks, models, art-review, screens, animation, three-to-og) are generated into the wiki as guide-<name>.md: `og api show <guide>` prints one, `og api find` returns their numbered sections (`testing §2`) beside the API entries, and `--kind guide` selects them. They hold the workflow, thresholds and pitfalls no signature states.

A jump goal whose arc the simulation owns: after `prepare` it takes off in the tick through an og.CharacterController's jump (jumpSpeed set for `height` under the controller's gravity, so ceilings and ledges are the controller's) or, without one, a fixed ballistic arc back to the takeoff height; the goal ends `recover` seconds after the landing tick, and the jump's state is in snapshots and the hash, with the landing each tick predicts from the controller's arc and the ground along it (og.motion state MOTION4; MOTION3 and MOTION2 saves still load). The motion model only draws it, its generated clip retimed onto that flight (docs/design.md §2.7, Jumps).

Check-bearing commands accept --require-checked to exit 1 when GPU checks remain unchecked; the default stays a warning. JSON summaries consistently expose uncheckedCount. og test retains its aggregate unchecked field as a deprecated alias; per-playtest unchecked remains a file list.

A* stays admissible (its heuristic at the cheapest cost). og.NavFilter is registered with the world only once a game inserts it, declares it in a system or hook, or restores a save holding it, so a world without it keeps its type table, saves and hash; run-time areas are in the og.nav state block's trailer (og_ecs::trailer, tag 2), written only when a mesh has one. Cooked navmeshes keep their blob version: areas are optional sections a blob without them loads as all ground.

Obstacle shapes beyond boxes: a box turned about +y (orientedBox), an upright cylinder and a convex prism, carved into a navmesh by id like og.nav.setObstacle (which stays the axis-aligned box and carves exactly as before). A shape blocks the cells whose centres it covers, grown by the agent radius, and rebuilds only its tiles; the shapes are in the og.nav state block's trailer, so a save restores them.

added.member: og.nav.setLink, og.nav.setLinkOpen, og.nav.finishLink, NavLinkDesc, NavLinkKind, NAV_ON_LINK, og.NavLinkReached, NavPath.links; type navmesh `link` (G2-4)
added.summary: Off-mesh links: a jump, a ladder, a door or a teleport from one point of a navmesh to another (both ways unless bidirectional is false), baked from a navmesh asset's `link` lines or set at run time by id. A* crosses an open link where it is cheaper than walking (cost in metres, 0 its length); a shut one (og.nav.setLinkOpen) is never planned and agents re-plan when it opens or closes. An agent reaching a link reports NAV_ON_LINK and sends og.NavLinkReached; the engine animates the crossing (an arc for a jump, half speed on a ladder, walking through a door, a teleport at once, or the link's duration), and a link with game (`traverse game`) holds the agent until og.nav.finishLink. og.NavLinkReached is registered only once a mesh has a link (or a save holding one is restored), so a world without links keeps its type table, saves and hash. Run-time links (where they moved from the baked ones) and agents crossing them are in the og.nav state block's trailer (tags 1 and 3); cooked links are an optional `links` section, so the navmesh blob keeps its version.

added.member: og.nav.load(world, path, profile?), NavMeshInfo.profile; type navmesh `agent <name>` (G2-4)
added.summary: Agent profiles: a navmesh asset may hold several agent blocks, each `agent <name> { radius height climb slope }` baked into its own mesh over the same geometry, areas and links, so a small body walks a doorway a big one cannot. og.nav.load takes the profile's name (omitted: the first agent block, the unnamed one if any) and refuses an unknown one naming those the asset has; NavMeshInfo.profile says which was loaded. The first profile fills the blob's own tables and each other is a whole navmesh blob in an optional `profile.<name>` section, listed in `profiles`: a navmesh of one unnamed agent cooks byte for byte as before and the blob keeps its version. A second unnamed agent, a repeated name or a name other than letters, digits, '_' and '-' is refused naming its line.

Crowd avoidance (ORCA, RVO2's construction): an og.NavAgent with og.Crowd { neighbours 8, horizon 2, obstacleHorizon 0.5, weight 0.5 } moves each tick at the velocity nearest what its path and steering want that keeps it clear of its nearest agents (G2-2's spatial hash: by distance, then entity) for horizon seconds and of the navmesh's boundary edges for obstacleHorizon, each pair of crowd agents sharing the avoidance by weight and an agent without og.Crowd avoided wholly. Deterministic by construction: every agent solves from the tick's start-of-tick state (a Jacobi step, so solving order does not matter) with + − × ÷ and sqrt only, and a symmetric jam (eight agents swapping across a ring lock still under plain ORCA) is broken by a per-agent margin of up to 5% of its radius from a hash of its entity id, the same on every host and run. og.Crowd is registered only once a game uses it (or a save holding it is restored) and adds no state block or trailer: an agent without it moves exactly as before (og.Steering separation), so existing nav games keep their hash. New projects start with it: create-game's templates that use nav (game's guard, third-person's sentinels, topdown's slimes) insert og.Crowd, which moves the game-3d golden replay from tick 84 (the guard keeps clear of the yard wall's edge); game-2d is unchanged. tower-defense keeps separation: its maze waves file in line, and ORCA let visitors pass each other beyond the towers' reach.

Children join in entity order; a changed child rebuilds the body; events and queries name the collider, and RaycastHit.body names its body. A world without such children steps and hashes exactly as before.
Every collider along a ray, nearest first (ties in entity order, alike on every host), at most maxHits (256).
The nearest point on any collider to a point within a reach, with its collider, body, outward normal, distance and whether the point is inside (solid or onto the surface).

added.member: Physics.sleepTicks, Physics.sleepSpeed, RigidBody.canSleep, RigidBody.sleeping, BodySlept, BodyWoke
added.summary: Sleep (G2-3): a dynamic body slower than sleepSpeed for sleepTicks ticks in a row sleeps, together with every dynamic body it touches (contacts and joints, transitively), and costs nothing until something wakes it: a body landing on it, a push, a joint, a moving kinematic body, a write to its components, its support going away, or sleepTicks set to 0. RigidBody.sleeping is written (write false to wake); BodySlept and BodyWoke are sent in entity order. Counted in ticks and saved with the world, never a clock. sleepTicks 0, the default, keeps every existing world stepping as before; og.RigidBody and og.Physics are version 2, and saves of 0.7.7 restore with the new fields at their defaults. Simulation: a world without sleep steps as before and its portable hash (og replay's, the golden replays') is unchanged; the raw world hash moves once for every engine world, because og.RigidBody's and og.Physics's new layouts are in the type table it covers. og.BodySlept, og.BodyWoke, og.JointBroken and og.ContactHook are registered with a world only once a game names them (a system or hook that declares one, an insert, a read of the events, a save holding one), like G2-4's lazy records: a world that never does keeps their absence from its type table, saves and raw hash, and the events are not sent to a world that cannot read them.

Breaking joints (G2-3): a joint whose solver load through a step passes breakForce, or whose torque about its anchor passes breakTorque, breaks: it is removed in joint entity order, its `broken` is written and og.JointBroken { joint, body, other, force, torque } is sent; writing broken false mends it where its bodies are. The load is what the solver holds through the step (a weight, gravity, what rests or presses on it); a lone impulse, applyImpulse or applyForce, is absorbed before it counts. 0, the default, never breaks; og.Joint is version 2 and saves of 0.7.7 restore with the new fields at their defaults. og.JointBroken is registered only once a game names it; a joint breaks (and `broken` is written) either way.

Contact hooks (G2-3) on a collider's entity: oneWay (solid only from one side, within 45°, what came in from elsewhere passing until clear: a platform jumped through from below), surfaceVelocity (a conveyor), friction and restitution in place of the pair's mean (negative keeps them), and ignore (up to eight entities, colliders or their bodies, it never collides with). The solver reads them from a table frozen at the start of the step, on its worker threads, so they are data rather than game callbacks, the same on both hosts and in replays. A world without hooks steps as before. og.ContactHook is registered only once a game inserts or names it; until then physics reads no hooks.

added.member: og.ai game actions, subtrees and utility (G2-4)
added.summary: Behaviour trees gain three nodes. `action <name> args` hands a long action to the game: og.ai sends og.AiActionStarted { entity, node, name, args } and the node stays running until og.ai.finish(world, entity, success, action?) answers it at the next think; when the tree leaves it first (a higher branch, a machine transition, og.ai.restart) og.AiActionStopped carries result AI_INTERRUPTED (new constant, 4). `use "<path>"` inlines another cooked behaviour's tree, its keys and routes joined (a differing route of one name, a machine, and a cycle are refused naming the chain; the cook's stamp covers every subtree reached, so editing one re-checks the trees using it; BehaviourInfo.subtrees lists them). `utility { inertia x; option <name> { score ...; nodes } }` runs the option whose score lines multiply highest (constants, or an input mapped by linear, inverse, quadratic, sqrt, smooth or step over a range), the running one gaining inertia, ties to the first written, failing when none scores above 0. Hash and save: the two events are lazy records, registered only once a behaviour with an action is loaded (or a save holding them restored); a finished action's pending result is og.ai's trailer section 1 (og_ecs::trailer), written only while one is pending. A game using none of this keeps its type table, saves and hash (the yard pin is unchanged).

added.member: Vehicle.model, VEHICLE_ARCADE, VEHICLE_DRIVETRAIN, Vehicle.gears, reverseRatio, finalDrive, idleRpm, maxRpm, torqueCurve, automatic, shiftUpRpm, shiftDownRpm, clutchTime, gear, rpm, handbrake, handbrakeGrip, driftGrip; og.VehicleWheel; WheelPose.entity; unit rpm (G2-3)
added.summary: A drivetrain car (G2-3): model VEHICLE_DRIVETRAIN drives the wheels with an engine whose torque curve (N·m at evenly spaced speeds up to maxRpm, 0 past it) goes through a gear's ratio and the final drive; the engine's speed follows the wheels while a gear is in and free-revs in neutral and while the clutch is out (clutchTime). An automatic gearbox shifts at shiftUpRpm and shiftDownRpm and into reverse when throttle is negative at a standstill; a manual one takes the game's gear. gear and rpm are written for a tachometer and an engine sound; the gearbox is in the og.physics state block's trailer (tag 4). Both models gain a handbrake that brakes the rear wheels and loosens their grip (handbrakeGrip), and driftGrip, their sideways grip while they slide. og.VehicleWheel children (up to 16, entity order) replace the four implicit wheels with wheels of their own radius, suspension, grip, steering share (negative for rear steering) and drive, brake and handbrake flags; vehicleWheels lists them with their entity. og.VehicleWheel is registered only once a game names it. og.Vehicle is version 2; saves of 0.7.7 restore with model VEHICLE_ARCADE, and an arcade car on its implicit wheels steps and saves exactly as before (tests/unchanged.rs).

added.member: SoftBody, SOFT_SPHERE, SOFT_BOX, SOFT_MESH, og.physics.softBodyPoints, SoftBodyPoints (G2-3)
added.summary: PBD soft volumes (G2-3): og.SoftBody is a closed surface of points (a sphere, a box or a closed mesh; 2D a ring) held by distance constraints along its edges (stiffness) and one constraint on the volume it encloses (pressure, volumeStiffness; 2D its area), dropped under gravity and pushed out of every solid collider with thickness and friction, so it lands, squashes and springs back; pinTop hangs it from its entity. It moves nothing, like og.Cloth. volume (now over rest) and center are written; its points are in the og.physics state block's trailer (tag 5), softBodyPoints reads them with the surface's triangles, and the renderer draws it with material. og.SoftBody is registered only once a game names it.

Weighted picks and shuffles on the engine's seeded streams: `weighted(weights)` draws an index with probability weight / sum (zero, negative and non-finite weights never picked; -1 when none is positive), `permutation(n)` is 0 to n - 1 in a Fisher-Yates order (n - 1 draws). A shuffled copy is `rng.permutation(a.length).map((i) => a[i])`. On og.Rng itself both need og.Rng among the system's writes.

added.member: og.procgen.noise, og.procgen.noiseGrid, og.procgen.poissonDisk, og.procgen.bsp, og.procgen.wfc, NoiseKind, FbmDesc, NoiseGridDesc, PoissonDesc, CellRect, BspDesc, BspResult, WfcTile, WfcCell, WfcDesc, WfcResult
added.summary: Procedural generation (G2-6): Perlin and simplex noise in 2D and 3D with fractal octaves, Poisson-disk points (Bridson), BSP rooms joined by corridors, and wave function collapse (the simple tiled model, with rotations, fixed cells and wrapping, retried on forks of the seed). Each is a pure function of its desc: it takes a seed (`world.resource(og.Rng)`'s value `.fork("label").seed`, a u32 as og.Rng's own) and draws only from og.Rng streams of it, in integer and IEEE f32 arithmetic with no host libm, so equal descs give bit-identical results on both hosts. They need no world and touch no state.

Writes a row-major block of cells at once (a generated grid mapped to tile ids): checked whole before any cell is written, a terrain layer re-tiled and the colliders rebuilt once, cells past the map's edge skipped.

`og relay` can play a bad network to test netcode against (G2-7): every frame to a peer held the latency plus up to the jitter in milliseconds, in order, and a send marked unreliable (lockstep's inputs) dropped the loss percentage of the time and free to overtake others, the draws from one seed.

Rollback netcode (G2-7): with mode `rollback` a tick runs on predicted inputs (each missing player's last input) up to maxPrediction ticks (default 8) past the last tick whose inputs are all in, and when a real input differs the world is rewound to the engine's own snapshot of that tick and re-simulated within the frame. A peer also predicts no further than it can re-simulate in half a frame. The zero value (`lockstep`) keeps today's behaviour; the confirmed world, which every peer agrees on, is the same as lockstep's for the same inputs.

resimulating(world) tells a system that the running tick is a rollback's re-run, so a game's own presentation (a shake, a haptic) fires once; finalHash(world, tick) is the shared hash of a tick's final world, run on real inputs only, kept for the last 1024 final ticks.

added.member: og.net.status: rollback, maxPrediction, confirmedTick, finalTick, acknowledged, predicted, rollbacks, resimulatedTicks, snapshotBytes
added.summary: The status reports the rollback state: how far the world runs ahead of its confirmed inputs, how many rewinds and re-simulated ticks it took, and the bytes the rewind ring holds.

A re-simulated tick plays each sound once: a play already sent for the same voice and sound is dropped, a new one is kept only if at most 100 ms late, and a voice the re-run no longer plays is stopped. Wall-clock presentation only: never in the tick or the hash.
og run's summary gives the confirmed (final) hash of its last tick in a room; in rollback the run continues past --ticks until that tick is final and acknowledged by every peer.

Tilemap orientations (G2-6): a map is orthogonal, isometric, staggered (odd rows shifted) or hexagonal (pointy- or flat-top, odd rows or columns shifted, sides half a tile), from a tilemap `.ogt`'s `orientation` line or a Tiled map (Tiled's isometric, staggered and hexagonal maps in that layout now cook; another stagger is refused naming the Map Properties to change). cellAt, cellCenter and the new neighbours follow it; an isometric or staggered tile's image stands on its cell's bottom (taller tiles overlap those behind, drawn back to front); solid tiles off the orthogonal grid collide as one collider per connected solid region (see TileLayerInfo.cellColliders), or one diamond or hexagon per cell on request (new Collider shapes 7 and 8, both profiles, also for game code); terrain layers need an orthogonal or isometric map. Cook: the orientation is an optional `orientation` section of the og.Tilemap blob, so an orthogonal map cooks to the same bytes under the same type hash and nothing re-cooks (pinned).

Run-time tilemaps (G2-6): create makes an empty map in code (size, tile pixels, unit, orientation, tileset asset ids, layers), with a handle from the world's own counter; resize grows or crops a map (a loaded one too), moving its cells, every placed copy's edits and its objects by (x, y), refusing an odd shift along a staggered or hex map's shifted axis. Both are world state: the og.tilemap block's og_ecs::trailer holds the maps made or resized whole (section 1, tilesets by asset id) and the counter (section 2), written only once a map was made or resized, so a world that only loads maps saves and hashes as before (pinned: tests/tilemap_runtime.rs). A save restores them in a session that never made them; an earlier save puts a resized loaded map back as loaded.

Merged tilemap colliders off the orthogonal grid (G2-6): each connected region of solid cells (sharing sides) is one static collider, a generated triangle mesh whose shape is saved with the world (a restore needs no mesh): in 2D its outline, a hollow polyline with holes as their own loops, in 3D the closed prism over it. A static map now costs physics per region, not per cell (256 × 256 hex, half solid: 1,264 colliders instead of 32,631; steady tick 0.26 ms against the merged orthogonal map's 1.73 ms, release). A layer's `cellColliders true` (`.ogt` layer line, Tiled bool property, TileLayerDesc) keeps one diamond or hexagon per cell. SHAPE_TRIMESH now works in 2D for game code too: the outline of the mesh's triangles. Cook: a layer flag bit, clear for every map cooked before, so nothing re-cooks.

Stall timeout, drop and rejoin (G2-7): a peer silent for a second is reported (og.PeerStalled, this peer's own), and past stallTimeout (5000 ms; 0 never drops) or on leaving the room its seat is dropped at a tick every peer agrees on (og.SeatDropped, hashed), with empty input from then on. With rejoin (default true) a dropped player that comes back, or a newcomer of the same name, takes its seat back from the authority's world (og.SeatRejoined, at one tick on every peer). The seat events are registered only once a world runs lockstep in a room.
The status lists the silent peers and counts the drops; each seat hold says whether it ended because its peer left the room or stalled.
og run's summary carries the game's facts (og.game's `facts`), as the probe prints them.
Coin Duel notes the seats changing hands (Duel.droppedAt, rejoinedAt, drops, rejoins), shows "Waiting for peer n" while a peer is silent, and takes `stall:<ms>` for og.Lockstep.stallTimeout.

added.member: og.i18n.formatCompact, og.i18n.formatCurrency, og.i18n.formatDate, og.i18n.formatTime, og.i18n.formatDuration, DateStyle, TimeStyle, DateFormat, TimeFormat; MessageFormat `{n, number, compact}`, `{p, number, currency/EUR}`, `{d, date[, style]}`, `{t, time[, style]}`
added.summary: Locale formatting (G2-6): compact numbers (`1.2K`, `1,2 Mio.`, `1.2万`), currency amounts with the currency's own symbol and fraction digits (`$1,234.50`, `1.234,50 €`, `￥1,235`, Indian grouping in hi), dates in four styles and times in two, and clock-face durations, in the active locale's digits and separators. A date or time is seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC that the game passes in, with an offset for formatDate and formatTime; nothing reads a clock, so the text is the same on both hosts and in a replay. A message's tables now format with their full tag (zh-TW writes Traditional), and `{n, date}` and `{n, time}` parse instead of being refused; `{n, number}` keeps its form.

added.member: og.TimeGroup, og.TimeGroups, og.time.setGroupScale, og.time.groupDt, og.ParticleSystem (time groups)
added.summary: Time groups (G2-6): og.TimeGroup puts an entity in one of 16 groups and og.time.setGroupScale sets a group's scale on top of the global one (0 freezes it); og.anim, flipbooks, 2D skeletons, the entity's scaled tweens and its og.nav agent advance by scaledDt times that scale, groupDt answers it for game code. Physics stays on the global scale (one solver steps every body), as do timelines and the UI. Both types are registered only once a game names either, so a world without them keeps its type table, saves and hash (pinned: og-runtime tests/time_groups.rs); a save of a grouped world restores its scales in a session that never named them.

added.member: og build --publish: content-hashed names and the service worker's incremental update
added.summary: A publish build serves its shell, engine Worker, audio worklet, engine glue and wasm (single-threaded and lanes) and the Basis transcoder as <stem>.<12 hex of sha256>.<ext>, cached for a year (_headers). The page finds them through og-config's files, and og-build.json gives them in worker, wasm, lanes, names and each source map's file. A new build's service worker copies every file, packs included, whose content its previous cache holds, and fetches only what changed (docs/web-export.md §Content-hashed names, §The shell). For the platform's checks the build keeps index.html's ./play.js, now a one-line loader of play.<hash>.js, and plain copies of origin-engine.js and origin-engine_bg.wasm. These aliases go away only once docs/platform-asks.md #18 has landed, in a later minor version with its own breaking entry; until then nothing a game or host reads changes.

added.member: og.load.imageData, og.load.gltfData, og.load.release, og.load.imageInfo, og.load.completions, og.load.replayCompletions, the dump_memory command, LoadBudget, ImageDataDesc, GltfDataDesc, ImageKind, ImageInfo, LoadCompletion
added.summary: Uncooked images and models at run time (G3-4): a PNG or JPEG, or a glTF 2.0 (.glb, or .gltf with data: URIs), that a player made or a generator wrote, loaded from bytes and drawn like a cooked texture or model (world.instantiate, og.Model, og.load.gltfInfo). Its size, a model's triangles and each image's dimensions are read from the headers and checked against LoadBudget (32 MiB, 500,000 triangles, 4096 texels, at most 8192) before anything is decoded; a load over a limit is refused at the call, naming the limit and the fix, and so is what the reader does not decode (Draco, meshopt, Basis, WebP, sparse accessors, another file). Natively a thread decodes images; on the web the browser does (createImageBitmap in the engine's Worker), so the engine thread never waits, and a model's primitives are converted a LoadBudget.frameMs at a time. Completion is host input: it is applied at a tick boundary, within LoadBudget.frameMs a frame, and journaled (og.load.completions), and og replay --record keeps the journal so --compare and og.load.replayCompletions put each load in place at its recorded tick. In a lockstep or rollback room a completion stays local to each peer: the game shares the bytes with og.platform.roomSend and agrees on the tick the simulation uses them through og.net.submit. og.load.release frees an uncooked asset: a pending load is dropped unjournaled, a ready one's textures and meshes are emptied under their handles (what still names them draws nothing), giving back their GPU memory and CPU copies; the command channel's new dump_memory[:path] writes the probe's memory report, the GPU figures included.

added.member: TransitionKind glitch; a style's motion `enter glitch <strength>` and `toast glitch <strength>`
added.summary: A glitch transition (the owner, for cyber): the content draws through the existing glitch layer material (slices pushed sideways, colours split) as it fades in or out, over 150 to 180 ms whatever the style's base duration, weakening as it settles. Any style or transition can name it. Its slices come from the element's id and the tick-counted UI clock, so a captured frame is the same every run; under reduced motion it is a plain fade.

added.member: og.StreamCell persist and budget, og.StreamAnchor maxSpeed, a scene's `stream "<name>" { cell }` group; dump_stream's hold and holds
added.summary: World cells, G3-3 batch 2: a `persist` cell keeps its entities as they are through an unload, in the og.cells state block (snapshots, saves, the hash and rollbacks carry it), and `budget` spreads a large cell's spawn over ticks (a 5,000-entity cell's worst tick 41/28/19 ms at budgets 1000/500/250, its one-tick load 153 ms). A sub-scene can declare a cell group, `stream "<name>" { cell; asset ... }`: its blob leaves the boot bundle for the group's pack, fetched ahead of each anchor by 2 s at its StreamAnchor.maxSpeed. A tick that would load a cell whose blob has not landed is held, never skipped or reordered, with each hold and its length in the engine's log and dump_stream's hold and holds; natively a read completes at once, so a native run never holds. A room session over anchorless cells is refused at its start. The og.StreamCell and og.StreamAnchor layouts grew, so a world with cells hashes and saves differently; a world without them is unchanged.

added.member: og.WorldOrigin, og.OriginShifted; the IDL attribute worldspace
added.summary: Large worlds, R12: a world that names og.WorldOrigin shifts as a tick starts once its focus (WorldOrigin.focus, else the first og.StreamAnchor, else og.Camera.position) strays past `step` from the zero, by the multiple of `step` nearest it, so every place stays near zero however far the world goes; the zero is kept in f64 and og.OriginShifted carries the delta. What moves is the schema's: fields marked `worldspace world`, `root`, `hook` or `none` with their axes (og-idl refuses an unmarked Vector2/Vector3 record field named as a place); every state block shifts, rapier's bodies in place with their contacts, warm starts and sleep kept, navigation by a frame offset, streamed cells with their subtrees; VirtualCamera.eased and CameraBrain.fromPosition are marked world. The render origin is laid on the absolute world's grid, so a shift draws nothing different. 2D worlds shift on plane xy. A world without og.WorldOrigin keeps its hash and frames.

added.member: texture { stream true }, model { stream_textures true }; the probe's mip_stream and dump_stream's mips
added.summary: Texture mip streaming, G3-3 batch 3: a texture cooked with `stream true` ships its mip tail (levels at most 256 px, byte for byte the whole chain's) in the boot bundle and its whole chain as `<id>#mips`, fetched on demand. Before each frame the engine measures how many pixels each streamed texture covers, loads the whole chain of the most magnified within a 128 MiB mip budget, swaps it in under the same handle and puts the tail back once the texture has been small for 120 frames; texture size reports the whole chain's throughout. Presentation only: a world's hash never depends on it. The probe's `mip_stream:resident` shows every streamed texture whole before each frame, for reproducible captures; `mip_stream:stream[:<MiB>]` streams within that budget. Textures without `stream true` cook and draw as before.

added.member: og.Decal normalMin, normalMax and normalScale; decals past 32 per frame

Existing decals draw as before; off by default (an empty normal region).
Up to 64 blendshapes: weights of targets 9…64, carried with the previous frame's weights for motion vectors.
An emitter's events (birth, death, collision) as an event gameplay reads; its systems are simulated in the tick. Emitters gain render mesh, lit, distortion, subEmitter and events lines.
Cloth on a skinned model's mesh, posed by the skin and simulated in the tick (R9).
An og.Garment's simulated points after the last step, in the world (R9).
Plays a clip on a model on the GPU from a shared baked clip, for crowds (R9).
An open sea: Gerstner waves of a fully developed sea for the wind, with swell and choppiness, whitecaps on the crests; og.physics.waterHeight reads the same surface in the tick (R5).
three.js Water2's flow map: the flow's direction per point, for the normal map's layers or the travelling waves (R5).

Floats a dynamic body on og.Water (a lake or a sea's waves) and og.WaterSurface by its voxelised hull: each cell under the surface lifts by the water it displaces at that cell, so hulls right themselves and pitch and roll with the waves, computed in the tick; submerged is written. Lazily registered: a world without it hashes as before.

A notice from the page that frames the game, outside any platform service: Player protocol 2 `platform` `{ notice: { kind: "host", data: { name, ... } } }`, applied at the next tick's start as og.PlatformNotice like the others. The engine gives it no meaning of its own; the game and its page agree what each name means (engine.origingame.ai's hero switches scenes with it). An appended variant: a game that never reads notices runs as before.

added.member: the built-in styles wasteland and foundry
added.summary: Two built-in UI styles of the sixteen packs (docs/ui.md §12.5), each painted from its approved sheet: wasteland (rusted riveted plate, duct tape, safety orange, a stencil display face; survival, crafting and extraction) and foundry (iron in brass rims, rivets, furnace orange, wide serif capitals; city builders, factory and 4X). A look names them with ui "wasteland" or ui "foundry"; og style list names them and og style new starts from them for their look families. Every other built-in style is unchanged.

New command: og frame measure <png> [--region x,y,w,h] [--against x,y,w,h] [--units px|fraction] [--metric contrast,highpass,mean,ramp] [--rows N] [--json] measures a region of any captured frame the same way on every machine, so a reviewer's numbers reproduce without image scripts: WCAG contrast (the ink, the region's darkest or brightest 5 %, against the median ground of --against or of the region), high-pass energy (the mean |grey - its σ 2 px Gaussian blur|, with its ratio to --against), the mean colour and grey, and the grey per band of --rows rows with the largest step. Reads the PNG's 8-bit sRGB values only; exit 2 on a usage error, 1 when the image cannot be read or the region lies off it.

project.ogt's screens {} takes any screen name: title, play and results are captured first, then the block's other screens in order, then the ui { screen } entries it does not name (before, a name other than title, play or results was refused, so nothing a game declared beyond them was captured). --sizes desktop,phone (also phoneLandscape, phonePortrait, tablet or WxH; phone follows publish { orientation }) captures every screen at each size into og-out/style/<screen>@<viewport>/; --size and the default (desktop 1280x720) keep og-out/style/<screen>/. --json adds to each frame its viewport, label (<screen>@<viewport>), size and the renderer tier that drew it; to contract its extends chain, the look's flattened art blocks (art, colours as sRGB hex), the palette's colours (palette.hex) and the catalogue style's checks and intended (style); and a coverage block (screens, viewports, uncoveredScenes: each scenes {} entry with no screen of its name, the start scene covered by play). --critic adds the style's intended traits and each frame's label (JSON: intended, shots); its frames list is unchanged. Additive: existing fields keep their meaning.

Each finding carries value, bar and unit where its rule measures a number (contrast's ratio against 3, 7 or the 4.5 warning bar; a text's size against its floor; a touch target's side against 44; an overlap's or overflow's area or px against 0) and at, one UiFindingAt per cell: the cell, its viewport, the box in CSS px (the overlap's rectangle, the text's line box, else the first path's element) and the cell's captured frame. check.json and --json list every cell's frame (frames), and --json names check.json (report). mergeFindings keeps every cell's place. Optional fields: findings built by older code still merge and print.

Every style entry has intended: one sentence, never naming the style, saying which traits of its frames look like defects and are the style (hard one-pixel steps, dither, broken edges, crushed-looking blacks), read by every critic beside the three checks (og-taste §12); the validator requires it. An added field: readers of the catalogue that ignore it read it as before.

The skill gains §5, the art bar a frame that passes every check is still held to (hierarchy, art, numerals, selection, depth, spacing, motion: each worded relative to the game's own look and decided by a number og frame measure, og ui check or og style check reproduces), and §6, verdicts: approve or hold, every hold a frame, a region, a criterion (style-check-N, bible:, contract:, measure:, bar:<item>), the measured value and what passes; a preference is a note, contrast is judged at the bar the engine's check states and never stricter, and a resubmission is judged on the held notes and regressions only. The skill keeps its name; its body is a new pack version. og-build §8, og-ui §8 and og-taste §12 describe the new measures.

Places the scatter's chunks with a compute pass when they come into range, by the same rules as the CPU (layer weight, holes, noiseThreshold, avoidWater, the footprints of the scatters placed before it) from the terrain's finest tiles, with nothing per copy on the CPU: on a moving camera over three chained scatters, 60.3 ms of CPU a frame drops to 14.3 ms for 0.21 ms of GPU. On by default; gpuPlacement: false places every chunk on the CPU. Where the renderer has no compute, or a footprint chain is too long or too wide, the CPU places them. The copies match the CPU's placement but for the last bits of the arithmetic: every scatter scene's reference frame (terrain-grass, terrain-grass-wind, terrain-hidden, terrain-scatter-unshadowed, impostor-scatter, probe-outdoor) holds within its tolerance, so a game draws as before. Visual only; the simulation is unchanged.

A `type flipbook` sheet takes animated GIF, WebP and APNG files (`source "hero_run.gif" { clip "run" mode loop fps 12 event 3 "step" align feet }`, a clip per file) instead of a texture: the cook decodes and composites the frames, keeps their delays as clip durations (10 ms or less shown as 100 ms, as browsers do), keys a flat background (`key auto|"#rrggbb" [tolerance]`, only what the border reaches, the edge ring unmixed), aligns the frames (`align feet|bbox|centroid|none`) in whole texels, resamples (`scale`), crops every frame to one size with the pivot at the anchor (`padding`), shares identical frames (`dedupe`) and packs them into the texture `<sheet>#sheet`, writing the same canonical sheet an Aseprite atlas makes.

`og sprite inspect <file.gif|.webp|.png|sheet.ogt> [--key auto|off|#rrggbb] [--tolerance T] [--out frames.png] [--json]` measures an animated sprite source, or a sheet built from them: frame count and delays, each frame's drawn bounds, centroid and coverage with their drift from the first frame, duplicate frames, the loop seam (last to first) beside the mean and largest frame-to-frame step, alpha levels and the edge fringe (edge and partial texels, the colour step to the interior and the distance to the background). Numbers only, no thresholds.

added.member: GraphDesc.sprite, og.AnimationGraph on og.Flipbook and og.Skeleton2D
added.summary: og.anim.graph(desc) with `sprite: true` builds a graph whose states name flipbook or rig2d clips; an og.AnimationGraph beside an og.Flipbook or og.Skeleton2D then drives it with the same states, parameters, transitions, interrupts and layers as a 3D skeleton. A flipbook cuts hard, only when the frame on screen ends (a transition's fade is ignored), keeping the phase within one state or sync group; a 2D skeleton cross-fades and blends its two heaviest leaves. The graph runs in the tick, its state is saved with the world and restored by snapshot. Off unless a graph is attached; existing games are unchanged.

A second clip sampled beside `clip` and mixed in by `blend` (0 to 1, slot draw order and attachments from the heavier clip); a graph sets them, a game may too. Defaults 0: the skeleton plays one clip as before.

fixed.summary: Ground snapping holds only a controller that was grounded at the start of its move (down slopes and steps), as rapier's own controller does: one falling from a jump or off a ledge now lands where it meets the ground instead of being pulled down to ground within snapDistance in one tick (up to 0.2 m at once by default, a visible drop at every landing).
A `type ui-material`'s `source` is read relative to the material file first, then from assets/, so a material installed with a kit keeps finding its WGSL.
The UI state saves which finger holds each touch control (version 16); a save at version 15 upgrades on load.
Ejecting a kit document copied the whole kit beside it (its TypeScript, manifest, skill and review sheet); it now copies the document with its companion documents and assets only.

On a phone in portrait the conversation's caption and choices traded room every tick and the caption rose over the tools; the choices now take a fixed share of the room. A resource bar laid in the flow folds to its box, not to the screen.

A restored grid or navmesh keeps the edit count its agents planned on. A restore rebuilds a mesh's obstacles, areas and links (or a grid's costs) with edits of its own, so its count only matched the saved paths by chance, and when it did not every agent planned again on the tick after a load (the same motion, a different world hash). The count is now set back from the saved paths; a nav edited after its newest path was planned also writes its count in the og.nav trailer (tag 4), so a path that was stale at the save is stale after it. A state whose paths are current saves byte for byte as before.

A save holds the names given since the last tick began: an entity named by world.spawn between ticks (GameDesc.start, a command) and then saved, or named by a system and saved by a later system in the same tick, restores with its name instead of losing it for good (a restore drops the names still queued for the world). A name given in a system now goes into the world when that system returns, with its spawn, so the world hash of that tick includes it (it used to from the next tick on).

An engine upgrade no longer refuses or resets a player's save: the engine migrates its own state in a save from an older build before the restore checks it (a table of steps by what moved and its version; og.ui's state block 9 -> 11, so a save from 0.7.7 restores without migrate, its game data, engine components and og.Rng record for record as this build runs the game).

The 512 KiB cap stays, measured against a 5,000-entity world (half physics bodies): 437 KiB, about 100 ms to save and 65 ms to restore natively; a slot's two banks are the platform's 1 MiB a player and game. A text over the cap is refused pointing at selections. Saves are og-save:2: (with the game's save version); og-save:1: saves still read, as version 1.

A save restores without `migrate` when an engine type (og.* component, resource or event) only gained fields since it was written: every saved field is still there with its type, and each added field takes its declared default from the IDL (og.RenderSettings' new fields in every save of the build before), never zero by accident. A removed, renamed or retyped engine field still needs an engine migration; a game's own types stay strict, refused naming the fields.

fixed.member: World.despawn/get/set/insert/remove/has/alive/nameOf, every API call taking an Entity, SpawnDesc.parent, world.spawn in a system
fixed.summary: A value that is not an entity number (null from world.find, undefined, a Result) is thrown naming the call and parameter on both hosts (`world.set: entity is null (world.find returns null when no entity has the name)`), not napi's conversion error natively or a coercion to 0 on the web; a non-number SpawnDesc.parent is refused instead of ignored; a dead handle is refused as `world.despawn: no live entity has the handle N`, with the hint `Archetype.entities holds (index, generation) pairs; use a.entity(i) for a handle` (and one engine log line per system and call) for a bare index; world.spawn's undeclared og.Parent or og.Transform write says spawn wrote it (`... (world.spawn with parent writes og.Parent; add og.Parent to the system's writes)`).

og-game (166 KB, 27 chapters) is an entry point of 40 KB; rendering, physics, 2D, animation and lockstep are the new skills og-render, og-physics, og-2d, og-anim and og-net, performance and video out are og-build, generators and type model og-model, looks og-taste. The API wiki is no longer mounted under og-game: every skill names og api show <module> for its modules, and api.ogt names the skill that teaches each module.

Keys held when the window loses focus or the page is hidden are released, and the pads come to rest with the keys they map to (the next poll sends a pad still held); nothing released them before, so a key could stay down in the game after an alt-tab.

A type whose layout changed since the save is compared only when the save holds data of it (a component row, a resource value or an event): a type it holds none of takes this build's layout, since nothing of it can be misread, so adding a field to a type a save never used (Model.variant) no longer refuses that save without migrate. Types the save holds data of are checked as before.

Automatic quality no longer cycles between two rungs on the GPU-time path: a rung that falls back within VERIFY_FRAMES waits twice as long before it is tried again and is given up after MAX_FAILURES, and the rung above is predicted with the measured spread added (meridian-loop at 2560x1600 stepped 1.6 to 1.7 and back every 30 s in Chrome and Edge).

A lockstep room no longer stalls for good when the room loses an input message: every input message carries all of the sender's inputs its peers have not acknowledged (each carries the sender's confirmed tick) and a peer waiting at a boundary sends them again. The lockstep wire version is 2: a peer on an older engine has its start refused with the reason instead of desyncing (G2-7).

fixed.member: lockstep: inputs overtaking a seat change
fixed.summary: An input message (sent unreliably) that overtook the reliable `admit` it followed let a peer confirm the new seat's first tick without it, so a late joiner's world could differ; input messages now name the seat changes their sender knows and wait for the resend otherwise. In rollback an admit's seat starts after every input the authority already sent.

fixed.member: og-net relay client: a stopped and resumed process
fixed.summary: A signal interrupting the client's socket read or write (a process stopped and resumed, a laptop waking) no longer counts as a lost connection.

A cooked font now carries U+00A0, U+2000-U+200A, U+202F and U+205F even when its file lacks them (or its charset leaves them out): empty glyphs with the font's own advance, else the width Unicode gives the space (the space's for U+00A0; en and em quads and spaces in em; figure and punctuation spaces as `0` and `.`; thin spaces and U+202F about a third of an em, never wider than the space; the hair space a tenth). They used to take no width, so CLDR's "3:05 PM" (U+202F before PM) drew as "3:05PM" and fr's "1 234" as "1234". The font's cook stamp moves ("font 2"), so every font re-cooks once; the blob layout and type hash are unchanged, and a requested `chars` space the file lacks is no longer reported missing.

A text drawing a character its face lacks (its atlas, and its file at run time) is warned of the same with or without a renderer, once per face and character, on the tick that drew it: og-ui reads each frame's texts against each face's metrics, og.render.text and og.render.floatingText are read when queued. Before, only a frame a GPU drew warned, so a run whose adapter request failed missed it (ui-kit's settings-saved, one run in five), and a character a second face lacked was never named.

added.member: og.PointerLock, og.Pointers.movement, PointerInput.movementX/movementY, og.PointerMove.movementX/movementY, InjectedInput pointerLock, mouse_move and pointer_lock actions
added.summary: Mouse-look: og.Pointers.movement is the mouse's relative movement this tick (movementX/Y of pointer 0's events summed, zero next tick); og.PointerLock { wanted, locked } lets a game ask for the pointer lock, which the web shell requests on the next press on the canvas, exits when wanted goes false and reports back from pointerlockchange (absolute positions held while locked). Injected pointer events and og.PointerMove carry movementX/Y (0 when omitted); the command channel's mouse_move:dx,dy and pointer_lock:on|off script them. Native runs are headless and never lock. Off by default; the simulation of existing games is unchanged.

og cook takes .mp3, .ogg (Vorbis) and .flac sounds beside .wav: decoded to 16-bit PCM in the cook (pure Rust, symphonia; no ffmpeg or afconvert) and encoded to QOA like a WAV, chunked and streamed the same way, under the source's asset id (audio/theme.mp3, audio/theme.mp3#chunk3). An undecodable file is refused naming the file and its format. The cook only: the runtime and the wasm are unchanged.

fixed.summary: The built-in look presets and style assets (og_cook look STYLES, BUILTINS) are statics, so og carries each CJK font once instead of twice (about 9.7 MB less per platform).
"What works" says the cited examples/* games live in the GitHub repository, not the installed package, and that the archetypes are installed (og new --archetype).

added.member: og api find / og api show
added.summary: Look the API up one entry at a time: og api find <words> lists the reference entries matching the words (name, module, first sentence, then field and parameter docs), one line each; og api show <name> prints one entry in full (signature, fields with defaults, ranges and units, doc) without its IDL source. Both read the wiki of the installed engine package. og-core §7 and og-game §25 teach them.

added.member: UI style fonts cjk and cjkDisplay
added.summary: A style's fonts block takes cjk and cjkDisplay, Simplified Chinese companions that set a label's Chinese beside the role's Latin face, ahead of the locale's fonts. Every built-in style names one matched to its Latin (templates/styles/cjk: Noto Sans SC, Noto Serif SC, ZCOOL KuaiLe, Fusion Pixel; OFL), cooked in only for a game with a zh string table, rendered at run time.

added.member: UI style tone <part> r g b a
added.summary: The frame art's centre colour (og cook measures it from the atlas when a style does not set it): a button's label ink, and the ground any widget reads through it, are judged against it at 7:1.
og.ui: warns when a control is laid out past the screen's edge with no scroll container to bring it back, naming it and by how much.

fixed: Button labels read on what is drawn: a game's primaryColor over a dark neon or scifi body keeps a light label, and a mid-scale colour (crimson) moves away from its ink as little as it takes. The accent highlight now follows the game's primary and reads 5:1 on its wash. Games on a built-in style look different.
A centred or end-aligned label in a column takes the column's width (it sat at the start in a box as wide as its text).

The neon style: its glow marks the button and the title only (no panel, HUD or number glow; tighter tube halos, a fainter grid), and its numbers are Chakra Petch SemiBold (Orbitron read 0 as Ø and 1 as 7).
AnchorDesc.margin's doc says it insets every edge; no IDL member added or removed.

added.summary: With the variable set (Origin Runner sets it when Origin Desktop draws the Session's engine), og run and og dev show their frames in the desktop window through shared GPU memory and render at the size the window asks for; without it nothing changes.

fixed: level-texturing's texture-level.ts paints with gemini-nano-banana-2.1 by default (qwen-image-2.1-pro stays one --model away); its http provider sends Qwen's seed and prompt_extend only to Qwen models and the view's size to the others, which Gemini's route requires; a resumed run keeps its model.

added: MaterialStyle.shadowDarkness (0 to 1, 0 off): where the sun does not reach (the toon ramp's dark band, the side turned away, a cast shadow) a lit surface loses that share of the sun and of the ambient light, so 1 draws shadows as solid black masses; local lights, emissive and shadowTint still show. RenderCapabilities.stylise names it shadowDarkness.

The cook paints a model's own colour textures with the look's Stylise paint fields in texel space (Kuwahara along the edges, bleed, pigment pooling, canvas grain), as it paints 2D sprites, when the project's look has an art contract that conforms models; textures no model claims, normal and data maps are not painted. Painted 3D textures re-cook and their frames change (painterly-3d, sculpted-clay, paper-craft on their samples).

The cook holds a model that says `conform character` (its type model text, or a glTF's import settings) to ArtShape.characterFaces, as a skinned one, and og style check judges it so; a type model past its face budget is built again with fewer segments before it is decimated.

MaterialStyle.surface (MaterialSurface none, clay, paper, plastic), surfaceStrength and surfaceScale: a made surface on every lit standard material (normal detail, colour grain, wrapped light and roughness in the mesh's own space), none by default; the sculpted-clay, paper-craft and miniature-diorama presets set it and their frames change.
fixed: The heavy-ink-shadows preset draws its shadows as solid black ink (MaterialStyle.shadowDarkness 1; shadowTint at amount 0 had no effect, and posterize never reaches black because the ambient light lifts every shadow), with a near-black sky, a blood-red haze and muted colour. Its frames change.

The low-resolution-3d preset ends its draw distance in a short dark fog the colour of its sky (the clear colour), so the 240-line frame reads as early-console 3D; its vertex snapping and affine texturing were already drawn. Its frames change.

MaterialStyle.surface no longer draws black blots where a mesh's shading normal lies in its face (a smooth silhouette or a rim turning away): the bump fades out there and the normal stays, instead of a NaN the post effects spread. Rumpus Isle's look sets surface none to keep its own colours under miniature-diorama.

The cook's mesh conformance (ArtShape.normals flat) drops faces thinner than the position grid and keeps flat normals on lathe poles and on voxelised parts turned by their placement; conformed models re-cook (model desc conform-mesh-v3).
RenderScene::set_shader_param writes a changed parameter into the material's uniform in place and keeps its bind group, instead of rebuilding both; frames are unchanged.

Stylise.dither and ArtPalette.dither bayer4 and bayer8 use the dispersed Bayer matrix; they drew a quadrant-clustered one whose tones showed as blocks of the matrix's size. Frames and cook-conformed textures dithered with them change; bayer2 does not.
The rubber-hose-animation and gothic-contour presets no longer posterize: per-channel steps turned their sepia and blue-grey art into olive, pink and violet bands. Their frames change.

breaking.change: A project whose look (project.ogt look, or one extending a preset) sets art blocks now cooks its assets conformed to them: 2D art to the pixel grid, the palette and the line (and, with stream A3, models, mesh textures and clips to the shape, texel and motion contract). Frames of such a game change. With stream A4 such a project (one naming its look in project.ogt) also draws under the contract's runtime defaults: cleanEdge pixel-art rotation, the line on sprites the cook did not line, ArtCamera's preset on an applied look, ArtMotion.stepFps as the animation step. At run time, a look with art blocks also sets the camera from ArtCamera when applied, defaults Sprite.outline from ArtLine, draws pixel art through cleanEdge under ArtPixels.rotation cleanEdge, and defaults AnimationPlayer.stepFps from ArtMotion.stepFps, which changes the ticks of a game whose animation drives play (rubber-hose-animation, sculpted-clay).
breaking.fix: Keep it (the style is the point), or opt an asset out with conform off in its import settings or project.ogt conform { off ... }, or set the preset's art blocks to zero in the game's look. At run time: a player whose own AnimationPlayer.stepFps is above 0 keeps it, and ArtMotion { stepFps 0 } in the game's look turns the default off; the camera preset is applied with the look, before GameDesc.start, so camera code in start or later wins.

added.summary: New resource (module art): the palette the assets' texels sit on: colors, strict, maxColors, rampSteps, accents, dither; no constraint at zero.
New resource: the pixel grid of 2D art: unit, logicalHeight, spriteSizes, rotation, rotationSteps, snap; no constraint at zero.
New resource: texel density on 3D surfaces: density, maxSize, filter, mips; no constraint at zero.
New resource: the shape language of models: propFaces, characterFaces, normals, normalAngle, bevel, voxel, silhouette; no constraint at zero.
New resource: the line the assets carry: width, color, place, distanceFalloff; no line at width 0.
New resource: stepFps, maxFrames, squash; no constraint at zero.
New resource: projection, fixedAngle, pitch, yaw, fovMin, fovMax, pixelPerfect; no constraint at zero.
New enum: free, nearest, cleanEdge, prerotated.
New enum: any, nearest, linear.
New enum: any, full, none.
New enum: any, smooth, flat, angle.
New enum: outside, inside, both.
New enum: any, perspective, orthographic.
Left out or empty, project.ogt's look "looks/<id>.ogt" line is applied when it has one; the two naming different looks is refused. A project without the line runs as before.
Names the art resources a look sets too.
Inside a system, an art resource the system does not declare among its writes is left as it is instead of refusing the look.
A look's blocks include the seven art resources, checked against their records as the frame's are; the 37 presets carry their catalogue style's values.
project.ogt's look "looks/<id>.ogt" names the look whose art contract the cook reads before any asset cooks; create writes it beside GameDesc.look.
The brush the cook draws a 2D line with (og.ArtBrush); diamond at zero.
New enum: diamond, circle, square.

The cook conforms sprites, flipbooks, tile sets and UI images to the look's art contract (pixel grid, 1-bit alpha, Oklab palette with dither, line, prerotated cells, painted 2D) and writes <id>#index for palette swaps; conform off and project.ogt conform { off } opt out; og cook --report lists every change. Byte-identical without a contract.

Knowledge (scripts/brief.ts) and @origingame/create-game: artBrief(look, kind, subject, options?) compiles the flattened look and its catalogue entry into the request for one asset: prompt, references, generator parameters; readLook(dir) and presetLook(slug) read a look from disk. A public contract (docs/art.md §2.2).

og style check [project] [--title|--play|--results <commands>] [--size WxH] [--no-frames] [--critic] [--json]: every cooked asset measured against the look's art contract (palette hit rate within ΔE00 2, colours, pixel grid and half pixels, line, texel size, filter and mips, faces against the budget, flat-normal share, texel density and spread), every opt-out listed, and the title, play and results frames (project.ogt's screens block) measured; --critic prints the catalogue's three checks and the frames only. og doctor --project has a style line; og build --publish prints it as warnings, never refusing.

A pixel outline this many logical pixels wide (0 to 4), drawn by the sprite shader from the texture's alpha; 0 is none, or under the project's art contract the look's ArtLine.width for a texture the cook did not line.
The outline's linear colour; at its default, the art contract's ArtLine.color.
A palette swap: the sprite draws its texture's index texture (the cook's <id>#index) through a row of this palette texture of N rows; 0 is none.
The row of Sprite.palette drawn.
A palette swap of every tile layer through a row of this palette texture; 0 is none.
The row of Tilemap.palette drawn.

Under project.ogt's look (stream A4): ArtPixels.rotation cleanEdge draws pixel-art textures through the new cleanEdge sampler (og-render TextureFilter::CleanEdge), ArtLine defaults Sprite.outline, ArtCamera sets the camera's projection, angle and field of view when a look is applied and pixelPerfect snaps the 2D camera by logical pixels, ArtMotion.stepFps defaults AnimationPlayer.stepFps, and a strict ArtPalette tints the UI's icons to their nearest palette colour. Without the look line nothing changes.

added: Knowledge: the craft skills architecture-discipline, component-forge, level-texturing (with scripts/texture-level.ts), localization, recipe-craft and visual-acceptance move from origin-agent into the knowledge package under the same names, free of platform tools and pointing to the og-* skills and the wiki for the API; texture-level.ts's providers are handoff (default), http (an OpenAI-compatible image endpoint) and dashscope, and runs that say agent or gateway resume.

Knowledge: payload(roots) and defaultRoots(pkg?) of knowledge/scripts/lib.ts, with the PayloadFile and Roots shapes, are a public contract beside installed, mount and summary: the platform reads the knowledge straight from the installed package with payload(installed(dir).roots). Nothing about them changed.

fixed: og check on a TypeScript install that bun x left incomplete (tsgo, where tsrs has no package): instead of tsgo's Go panic or Cannot find global type errors, it names the incomplete directory and the fix (delete it or bun pm cache rm, then rerun); og doctor reports it as broken.

The knowledge package's scripts/mount.ts CLI mounts into an origin-agent checkout's knowledge/, where the platform's knowledge moved from OriginGame's packages/game-knowledge/production; installed, mount and summary are unchanged.

og-ui glass on WebGL2 in Chrome and Edge on Windows blurs as on metal, WebGPU and DX12: each pyramid level took its tap spacing from textureDimensions of a view whose base mip level is that level, which ANGLE on D3D11 answers with level 2b's size for base level b, so the blur was about twice as wide. Each level of the glass pyramid and of a view's glow chain now takes the size it reads from a uniform; native frames are unchanged.

WebGL2 starts about four times faster on Windows (ANGLE on D3D11): programs link in the background with KHR_parallel_shader_compile, read when a pass first draws with them, and the GL tier's lit programs leave the rect-light (LTC) code out until a scene has a rect light. fx-showcase's cold first frame went from 30.4-31.7 s to 7.0-7.5 s in Chrome 155 and from 30.3-31.2 s to 7.6-7.7 s in Edge 155; WebGPU, metal and DX12 are unchanged and no frame moved. The trade-off: on WebGL2, a scene that gets its first rect light during play links its lit programs again at that moment (about 5 to 8 s on ANGLE D3D11, waited for by the next lit frame); to pay it at load instead, put an og.RectLight in the first scene (one at intensity 0 counts).

added.summary: og bake projection init|plan|prepare|project|holes|export --run <dir>: a gray level glb painted from planned views by an image model the caller runs, projected into one texture and exported as a textured glb, on the CPU.

fixed: A NavAgent with faceMovement turns the same on every host: its turn was glam's slerp on the host's sinf and drifted by up to 16 ulp between Windows and Linux for the ticks of a turn; it is now a yaw step through og-core's deterministic math, so the turning ticks' quaternions move by an ulp on every host.
og.terrain.sample's slope is computed with og-core's deterministic acos instead of the host's.
